name: Multipolar World — 2010
description: Dated geographic atlas sandbox (2010-01-01). Capitals use geographic coordinates; modern province boundaries are clipped to dated national borders; historical internal divisions are approximate. Colonial control follows an explicit scenario overlay.
worldContext: Start: 1 January 2010. Governments are dealing with the aftermath of the global financial crisis in an interconnected world of trade, finance and international institutions. Diplomacy, energy, infrastructure, public opinion and communications matter alongside military capacity. Nuclear deterrence makes escalation between nuclear powers qualitatively different from conventional war. States have distinct interests even inside alliances; NATO, the EU and the UN are not a single government. Do not import knowledge of later uprisings, wars, pandemics or election outcomes as completed facts or inevitable events. Model reform, procurement and institutional change with realistic implementation delays. Existing campaign outcomes override the historical starting trajectory.
simulationRules: Orders are queued immediately and their practical consequences are simulated during time advancement. Do not approve, partially approve or reject orders as a separate process. Explain unfulfilled intentions through events and concrete obstacles. There are no numerical treasury, stability, war-support, political-power or manpower mechanics. Judge capacity qualitatively from history, logistics and elapsed time. Never invent starting tracked formations; create them only from explicit player orders. Map colonies and dependent administrations are not automatically sovereign states. Respect actual diplomatic autonomy. Later historical events are possibilities, never mandatory scripted outcomes. Persisted campaign events and diplomacy override the starting briefing. Include exact geographic event locations when known; use null when uncertain.
